My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

messages.preview: Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

blocks.text:
Two failures:

1. **Rotation test**: expected `['3.json']`, got `[]` — all three deleted. Why? My sweep triggers when `_bytesSinceSweep >= maxBytes` — with maxBytes=1 every write sweeps; the sweep deletes files while `total > maxBytes`. After writing 3.json, total is (1.json + 2.json + 3.json) > 1 → oldest-first delete: 1, 2, then 3?? total after deleting 1 and 2 is still > 1 (3.json's size), so 3 gets deleted too. The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. Why didn't the sweep run? `_maybeSweep`: `_bytesSinceSweep < maxBytes && !hourElapsed` → hourElapsed is true (31 days), so sweep SHOULD run... unless `_lastSweepAt` was set on write 1 — no: after write 1, `_maybeSweep` runs (hourElapsed: last==null → true) → sweep at t0 (nothing to delete — 1.json age 0) → `_lastSweepAt = t0`. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). Real now is 2026-ish; my test clock says 2026-01-01 → 1.json's real mtime is "now" (2026-xx actual date, later than 2026-01-01?) → age = now(clock) - mtime(real) = negative → not expired. I need `env.setMtime(path, ms)` (test-only helper, saw it at memory_execution_env.dart:236). Fix the test: after write 1, setMtime 1.json to the fake t0; keep clock consistent.

Also fix 1 (newest survives). Update enforceBudget: skip index 0 (newest = last in oldest-first sorted? no — sorted oldest-first, newest is LAST). Delete only from the front, and stop before deleting the last remaining file: `for (var i = 0; i < sorted.length - 1; i++)`. Even when ALL are expired, keep the newest (the blob the just-written summary points at... actually the newest at sweep time might not be the one just written if sweep runs later; but keeping the newest is the "keep last N" semantic — good).

Wait — the TTL test expects `['2.json']` — 1.json expired → deleted; 2.json (newest) kept. With "never delete newest": loop `i < sorted.length - 1` → 1.json deleted (expired), stop. Good.

Rotation test: writes 1,2,3 each ~2-3KB. After write 3: sweep; sorted=[1,2,3]; loop i<2: 1.json deleted (total>max), 2.json deleted (total>max — total now = size(3) > 1) → stop at i=1 (can't delete newest 3). Result ['3.json'].

Edge: what if expired files include the newest? Newest survives — acceptable (it's the live head; the next sweep after it ages will remove it).
Two issues: the sweep must never delete the newest blob, and the TTL test needs `setMtime` (memory fs uses the real clock). Fixing both:

The budget semantics: "keep last N MB" — the newest file must survive even if alone it exceeds the budget. Fix: never delete the NEWEST file (skip it in the sweep). Standard rotation: delete oldest files until total fits OR only the newest remains.

2. **TL test**: `1.json` should be expired (written at t0 with clock t0; clock moved to t0+31d; write 2 happens at t0+31d — 1.json age = 31d > 30d TTL → delete). Got both files. At write 2: hourElapsed = 31d ≥ 1h → sweep runs. enforceBudget: ttl 30d, 1.json mtime = t0, now = t0+31d → expired → remove. So why did it stay?

Hmm — MemoryExecutionEnv mtime: does writeFile set mtime = wall clock NOW or the test clock? The store's clock seam returns my fake `current`, but MemoryExecutionEnv's file mtime uses the REAL clock (DateTime.now). ```dart
rig(turns, {bool requestBlobs = true, bool wireDump = false})
run 'go', settle 2, exit.
- default: session jsonl model_request_summary line → contains '"spillFile"' and NOT '"blocks"'; blob file <sid>/requests/1.json exists; blob detail (readDetail) has blocks + previews; seq increments for second summary (2.json).

``

How do turns map to request events? Each provider call emits one ModelRequestEvent. Scripted: toolTurn + textTurn → 2 requests. The first request's summary precedes the first assistant message. The rig's `_setle(rig, 2, ...)` waits for 2 provider calls.

For kill-switch: AgentCliConfig(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false). For default: omit (default true once implemented).

Now — IMPORTANT subtlety for the CLI: `_onModelRequest` writes the spill BEFORE appending records. The store's session id: `() => _session?.cachedId`. In the rig, the session exists by then. Good.

Test plan for `test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart`:

```dart
rig(turns, {bool requestBlobs = true, bool wireDump = false})
run 'go', settle 2, exit.
- default: session jsonl model_request_summary line → contains '"spillFile"' and NOT '"blocks"'; blob file <sid>/requests/1.json exists; blob detail (readDetail) has blocks + previews; seq increments for second summary (2.json).
- kill switch: requestBlobs false → summary line contains '"blocks"'; not spillFile; no .fah/trajectories dir in env.
- wireDump + spill: jsonl has NO trajectory_wire_dump record; blob carries wireDump; summary has wireDumpHash.
- wireDump + kill switch: jsonl HAS trajectory_wire_dump record (legacy inline) — byte-identical legacy.
``

How do turns map to request events? Each provider call emits one ModelRequestEvent. Scripted: toolTurn + textTurn → 2 requests. The first request's summary precedes the first assistant message. The rig's `_setle(rig, 2, ...)` waits for 2 provider calls.

One issue: the tool turn requires shell (`bash` call) — FakeShell with stdout ''. Fine.

For the summary line search: `raw.split('\n').firstWhere((l) => l.contains('"model_request_summary"'))` — the FIRST summary line (request 1). But with spill, the FIRST request's record is light already. Good.

Also: the JSONL contains `"blocks"` substring only if blocks persisted — the summary is the only record carrying blocks; system prompt blob records don't have "blocks". Tool manifests have `schemaJson`... no "blocks" key. Safe.

For kill-switch: AgentCliConfig(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false). For default: omit (default true once implemented).

Now — IMPORTANT subtlety for the CLI: `_onModelRequest` writes the spill BEFORE appending records. The store's session id: `() => _session?.cachedId`. In the rig, the session exists by then. Good.

Second subtlety: the `_trajectoryBlobPersister` dedups prompt/manifest blobs per session — with spill, recordsFor is still called with promptBlob/manifestBlob; unchanged.

No git hooks configured in this environment (CI enforces). Suite still running — dart test on this repo with all the PTY/integration tests takes a while. Let me use the waiting time to double-check a few behaviors by writing a quick sanity review of my store code once more, particularly:

1. `_maybeSweep` — `hourElapsed` computed with `last == null || ...` — on the FIRST write last is null → sweep runs immediately (a listDir on a fresh dir). Slightly wasteful but harmless (dir empty → 0). But on EVERY new store instance (per process) the first write sweeps once — fine.

2. `write` failure path: counter incremented even on failure — leaves a gap in numbering (1.json missing). Harmless.

3. Counter probe: `if (_counter == 0) { _counter = await _maxExistingSequence(sid); }` — inside the session-change guard: after a session switch, `_counter = 0` then probe. But careful: `if (_counter == 0)` after `_counter++`? No — the probe happens before increment; after probe `_counter` could be 0 (empty dir) then `++` → 1. Good.

4. In the CLI, the store is keyed to `_coreToolEnv` and never reset per session — `sessionId()` lazy per write handles the switch (counter resets via `_counterSession != sid`). Good.

5. `_sessionId` change also invalidates `_lastSweepAt`/`_bytesSinceSweep`? Those are global to the store; crossing sessions just keeps the sweep cadence — acceptable.

Now, one more potential fallout: `test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` or others that pin session JSONL byte shape from a REAL AgentCli run. Those runs now produce `spillFile` in summaries + `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/*.json` files in the env. Tests asserting exact record sets could see extra files but usually assert on JSONL content only. The suite will tell.

Also — headless/seal tests use `JsonlSessionStorage` on real envs; spill writes create files in temp dirs — harmless.

One REAL risk: tests that run AgentCli with a session open from `MemoryFileSystem` and then LIST the env root expecting specific entries (e.g. `.fah` dir assertions). We'll see.

While waiting — the `session_ephemerality` rule: I must keep working, not park. Let me review the diff so far for style/lint.

3. Counter probe: `if (_counter == 0) { _counter = await _maxExistingSequence(sid); }` — inside the session-change guard: after a session switch, `_counter = 0` then probe. But careful: `if (_counter == 0)` after `_counter++`? No — the probe happens before increment; after probe `_counter` could be 0 (empty dir) then `++` → 1. Good.

4. In the CLI, the store is keyed to `_coreToolEnv` and never reset per session — `sessionId()` lazy per write handles the switch (counter resets via `_counterSession != sid`). Good.

5. `_sessionId` change also invalidates `_lastSweepAt`/`_bytesSinceSweep`? Those are global to the store; crossing sessions just keeps the sweep cadence — acceptable.

No git hooks configured in this environment (CI enforces). Suite still running — dart test on this repo with all the PTY/integration tests takes a while. Let me use the waiting time to double-check a few behaviors by writing a quick sanity review of my store code once more, particularly:

1. `_maybeSweep` — `hourElapsed` computed with `last == null || ...` — on the FIRST write last is null → sweep runs immediately (a listDir on a fresh dir). Slightly wasteful but harmless (dir empty → 0). But on EVERY new store instance (per process) the first write sweeps once — fine.

2. `write` failure path: counter incremented even on failure — leaves a gap in numbering (1.json missing). Harmless.

3. Counter probe: `if (_counter == 0) { _counter = await _maxExistingSequence(sid); }` — inside the session-change guard: after a session switch, `_counter = 0` then probe. But careful: `if (_counter == 0)` after `_counter++`? No — the probe happens before increment; after probe `_counter` could be 0 (empty dir) then `++` → 1. Good.

4. In the CLI, the store is keyed to `_coreToolEnv` and never reset per session — `sessionId()` lazy per write handles the switch (counter resets via `_counterSession != sid`). Good.

5. `_sessionId` change also invalidates `_lastSweepAt`/`_bytesSinceSweep`? Those are global to the store; crossing sessions just keeps the sweep cadence — acceptable.

Now, one more potential fallout: `test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` or others that pin session JSONL byte shape from a REAL AgentCli run. Those runs now produce `spillFile` in summaries + `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/*.json` files in the env. Tests asserting exact record sets could see extra files but usually assert on JSONL content only. The suite will tell.

Also — headless/seal tests use `JsonlSessionStorage` on real envs; spill writes create files in temp dirs — harmless.

One REAL risk: tests that run AgentCli with a session open from `MemoryFileSystem` and then LIST the env root expecting specific entries (e.g. `.fah` dir assertions). We'll see.

While waiting — the `session_ephemerality` rule: I must keep working, not park. Let me review the diff so far for style/lint.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
pr_base_branch.txt

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

arguments.content:
### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
