{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

- name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,

imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:

  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a

  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

- name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

flowchart LR

  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

flowchart LR

  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```

- name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

flowchart LR

  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json]
  STORE -->|strip| REC[model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT[TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept]
```
</details>

### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[".fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json"]
  STORE -->|strip| REC["model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile"]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT["TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept"]
```
</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes and rotates the blobs with the ticket's policy: default 50 MB per session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first, newest always kept; sweeps fire on budget crossing or hourly.
- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745

  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]

{"content":"### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745

{"content":"### What changed
- Marathon-session `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: the per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump now spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`, and the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.

- Wired into both persist hosts (CLI `_onModelRequest`, app `AgentService._persistModelRequest`); `/trajectory inspect` names the request blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON with a strict-config kill switch — `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (plus `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically, mirroring the `spills:`/`images.registry` kill-switch convention.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path (the capture is never lost, never a crash), same AC6 shape as tool-result spilling.
- The record stays replay-safe: `TrajectoryRequestDetail.fromJson` picks up `spillFile`; the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` estimation basis survives the stubbing; old sessions (and dropped records, per the gh-1073 repair contract) render as before.
- `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the BLOB payload; the JSONL record becomes O(1KB) per request regardless.

        run: |

- name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in

        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
